req.title: Login case-sensitive username
req.statement: The system shall treat usernames as case-sensitive on POST /auth/login.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that usernames are case-sensitive on POST /auth/login. The pre-loaded database has user 'Rahul' (id=1, password='stone'). To verify case-sensitivity we must: (1) confirm exact-case login succeeds with HTTP 302 redirect (positive/EP), (2) confirm wrong-case username fails with HTTP 200 and error message (negative/NEG), (3) confirm a single-character case difference at the boundary of the username string is rejected (boundary/BVA). We also add a Decision Table test covering all combinations of case variants to kill boolean/comparison mutations. The login view returns 302 on success and 200 with flashed error on failure — we assert exact status codes and exact error text to maximise mutation kill rate.

tests.name: test_login_exact_case_succeeds

Flask test client initialised with TESTING=True
trace: R-FLASKR-036: correct case username must authenticate successfully
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

def test_login_exact_case_succeeds():
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/'

test_login_exact_case_succeeds()

Flask test client initialised with TESTING=True

tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

def test_login_case_sensitivity_decision_table():
    client = app.test_client()
    fail_cases = [
        ('rahul', 'stone'), ('RAHUL', 'stone'), ('rAHUL', 'stone'),
        ('anjali', 'cloud'), ('ANJALI', 'cloud'), ('aNJALI', 'cloud'),
        ('ishaan', 'stone'), ('ISHAAN', 'stone'), ('iSHAAN', 'stone'),
    ]
    for uname, pwd in fail_cases:
        r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': uname, 'password': pwd})
        assert r.status_code == 200, f'Expected 200 for {uname!r}, got {r.status_code}'
        assert b'Incorrect username.' in r.data, f'Expected error for {uname!r}'
    pass_cases = [('Rahul', 'stone'), ('Anjali', 'cloud'), ('Ishaan', 'stone')]
    for uname, pwd in pass_cases:
        r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': uname, 'password': pwd})
        assert r.status_code == 302, f'Expected 302 for {uname!r}, got {r.status_code}'
        assert r.headers['Location'] == '/'

test_login_case_sensitivity_decision_table()

tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

def test_login_case_sensitive_no_redirect_on_wrong_case():
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'james', 'password': 'river'})
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert r.status_code != 302
    assert b'Incorrect username.' in r.data
    assert b'Incorrect password.' not in r.data
    r2 = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'James', 'password': 'river'})
    assert r2.status_code == 302
    assert r2.headers['Location'] == '/'

test_login_case_sensitive_no_redirect_on_wrong_case()
